**Rebuttal**

Debater A's own construction supports 2a. Placing an interior point p in the ear at v_i gives one hole: the hull minus v_i, plus p. A point placed just inside the shared edge v_i v_{i+1} lies in two ears, so it yields two holes: the hull minus v_i plus p, and the hull minus v_{i+1} plus p. Both are convex and empty. For every a ≥ 2, 2a > a + 1, so a + 1 cannot be the maximum.

A's upper bound is also unsupported. A admits this step is the least detailed part of the case, and nothing in A's text rules out two holes per interior point. The ear argument gives 2a as the ceiling.

The strongest objection is whether the 2a configuration creates an empty convex (k+1)-gon. The hypothesis a ≤ k/2 − 1 gives 2a + 2 ≤ k, leaving two buffer ears. I concede I have not fully verified this check. But A has not exhibited any violating (k+1)-gon, so the burden is on A to show one exists.

**Answer: 2a.**
